name: immudb
tagline: Immutable, tamper-evident database with cryptographic proofs, offering key-value, SQL and document APIs.
description: immudb is an append-only database from Codenotary in which every write is recorded in a Merkle-tree-backed log. Clients can verify inclusion and consistency proofs themselves rather than trusting the server. It exposes key-value, SQL (with a subset of the PostgreSQL wire protocol) and document APIs, keeps full history so you can query data as of any earlier transaction, and runs embedded in Go or as a server. It is a practical self-hosted replacement for QLDB-style audit ledgers. The licence moved to BSL 1.1 from version 1.9DOM.2, so check the use grant before offering it as a service.

pricing.notes: Free for production use within the BSL grant; Codenotary sells support and commercial products.

scale.notes: Single primary with asynchronous or synchronous replicas.

strengths: Client-verifiable cryptographic proofs that history was not altered
Time-travel queries over the full history of every key and row
Embeddable in Go or run as a server, self-hosted anywhere
SQL access through a subset of the PostgreSQL wire protocol
weaknesses: BSL licence since 1.9DOM.2 restricts some hosted uses
Storage only grows; deletes are logical
SQL dialect and Postgres compatibility are partial
useCases: Replacing Amazon QLDB with a self-hosted ledger
notIdealFor: High-churn data that must be physically deleted (e.g. GDPR erasure)
